course_name_original: Fundamentos De Ciencia De Los Materiales I (Tecnología Industrial / Mecánica) (Plan 2024) (68041039)
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Materials Science I (Industrial Technology / Mechanical) (2024 Plan)

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of material science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to materials science and engineering
Internal structure of materials. Crystalline systems
Defects in crystalline structure. Solidification of metals
Constitution of metallic alloys. Phase diagrams. Transformations
Properties of metallic materials. Mechanical tests
Ferrous alloys of industrial interest. Treatments, characteristics and applications
teaching_methods: Participation and use of synchronous tools in the virtual learning environment
Participation and use of asynchronous tools in the virtual learning environment
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, it is essential to obtain a 'Pass' in the laboratory practices, a minimum of 1 point in the phase diagram construction and interpretation exercise of the face-to-face exam, and a minimum of 2 points in the multiple-choice test part of the face-to-face exam. Finally, students must achieve a minimum overall grade of five points. Continuous assessment (PEC) grades are saved for the September examination period. Laboratory practice grades are saved for successive academic years.
